findings.title: A seeded round now refuses to open when ONE seed class has no anchor, where it used to plant the rest and name the class
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:172 and src/CLI/Rounds.jl:297 (the now-unreachable `isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): "` branches)
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:244 (the pre-existing total-failure refusal the new one duplicates and widens)
findings.before: `println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted (salt $(rec["seed_salt"]))", isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", "))` — the round opened, planted what anchored, and NAMED what did not.
findings.after: `if !isempty(skipped)` / `println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", "))` / `println(io, "         a skipped class is UNDEFINED in recall, so the denominator shrinks in silence;")` / `return 2`
findings.why_it_matters: Opening a seeded round is the ordinary workflow, and a seed anchor is a REGEX against a corpus that legitimately moves: any prose edit that retires the anchored sentence rots one class. Before this diff that cost one class of recall, named in the bank record and in the tally; after it, the whole instrument will not open until the consumer either rewrites `.gbg/seeds.toml` (a consumer commit, mid-workflow) or passes `--no-seed`, which the sibling refusal three lines up calls fatal in its own words: "a round that plants nothing measures nothing". So the escape hatch offered in the refusal's own text is the outcome the code elsewhere refuses. The stated ground is also contradicted by the contract it cites: `Recall.per_class` — not touched by this diff — documents `class => "UNDEFINED"` for every skipped one "(kept in the denominator and named, never counted as zero)", and `Rounds.bank` writes that map into the bank record (Rounds.jl:593,613) whence Passes.jl:846 copies it into the tally. The skipped class is therefore already visible in the round's own artefacts; the 'silence' the refusal exists to end is a shrunk AGGREGATE at most, curable by reporting, not by refusing to measure five classes because a sixth cannot be planted. Base already drew exactly that line: Rounds.jl:244 refuses when NOTHING plants and tolerates the partial case — the new gate erases a distinction the design made on purpose.
findings.description: The fix is wider than the defect. The defect (a class quietly absent from the denominator) is a REPORTING defect, and the round already carries the fact it needs: `skipped` is written to the ground truth and to the tally. Turning it into a hard exit 2 converts a recoverable, documented partial measurement into a blocked instrument, and leaves the old, now-unreachable 'skipped classes (anchor absent)' suffixes at Rounds.jl:172 and :297 as dead evidence that the tolerant path was deliberate. Nothing in the diff migrates existing consumer seed catalogues, and no flag exists to accept a partial plan: `--no-seed` is all-or-nothing.

"" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): "`.

findings.title: close now demands a build record only `gbg round build` can write — every round open at this commit, and every round built through prepare or pass open, is refused
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:152 and src/CLI/Rounds.jl:198 (prepare's builds, recording nothing)
test/rounds.jl:543-546, :656-659, :720-723, :1015-1022 (four existing round records re-baselined with a green build block)
findings.before: close's conditions ended at `dirty = [p for (_, p) in Git.porcelain(root) …]; isempty(dirty) || push!(fails, "the round's files are not committed: …")` — no build was consulted, and the docstring's list still reads "The conditions: the latest pass fully closed, no dead lane, the round's files committed, the stamps unchanged …".
findings.after: `if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS` / `b = get(rec, "build", nothing)` / `if b === nothing … push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round")` / `elseif b["code"] != 0 …` / `else moved = Git.changed_paths(root, "$(b["head"])..HEAD", Preflight.covered_paths(cfg)); isempty(moved) || push!(fails, "the recorded docs build is stale — …")`
findings.why_it_matters: Three verbs run the consumer's `docs_build` — `prepare` (Rounds.jl:152 and :198), `pass open` (Passes.jl:567) and `gbg round build` (Rounds.jl:317) — and only the last one now writes `rec["build"]`. A round whose LAST action was a green pass-open build, the sanctioned way to rebuild during a pass, is refused at close as having no build at all; so is every round already open when this commit lands, with no migration and no override flag. The staleness test then uses `Preflight.covered_paths` = `src`, `test`, `ext`, `docs`, `Project.toml` plus every `[paths]` entry — for this package that adds `instruments`, `catalog`, `policy`, `schema`, `templates`, `fixture` — so a commit that touches only `test/` or `catalog/` after a green build forces a full Documenter rebuild before the round may close, though neither enters the site. And because `build` now writes ROUND.toml, the build dirties the round directory, which close separately refuses ('the round's files are not committed'), so the closing sequence is build, commit, and hope nothing under the covered paths moved in between.
findings.description: The underlying defect is real — a red build rode through two graded passes — but the gate implemented is wider than it: it rejects rounds whose build WAS run and green (through prepare or pass open), rejects every in-flight round unconditionally, and treats any change under the audit's covered paths, not the docs surfaces, as invalidating. The narrow fix is to record the verdict at all three call sites, and to test staleness against the surfaces the build actually reads. The contract was also not updated where readers look: close's own docstring still enumerates the conditions without the build, and the guide's two close sections (instruments.md:83, :182) still say close needs 'no id open, no lane dead, the files committed and the stamps unchanged'.
findings.evidence: diff hunk @@ -1151,6 +1151,24 @@ adds the block quoted above; `Rounds.build` is the sole writer (`+    rec["build"] = Dict{String,Any}("code" => code, "head" => …)`); Passes.jl:567 `code = Rounds.run_under_round(cfg, round, cfg["package"]["docs_build"]; log)` is unchanged and records nothing; `covered_paths(cfg) = unique(vcat(["src", "test", "ext", "docs", "Project.toml"], String.(values(cfg["paths"]))))`; test/rounds.jl's four re-baselined records all hand close a hand-written green `build` block rather than exercising a stale or absent one.

findings.title: A consumer that set latex_source_globs now has docs/src and docs/ REMOVED from the hat's source surface — the key replaces the four surfaces instead of adding to them
findings.before: panel.js:86 `ALSO the AUTHORED SOURCE (read it with Read/Grep; quote findings at file:line): the docstrings under ${A.repo}/src/ and ${A.repo}/ext/, the pages under ${A.repo}/docs/src/, and the rationale documents under ${A.repo}/docs/.` — every consumer's `needs: source` hat read all four.
findings.after: `globs = String.(get(cfg["instruments"]["check-consistency"], "latex_source_globs", String[]))` / `a["source_globs"] = isempty(globs) ? ["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] : globs`, rendered by panel.js as `under: ${A.source_globs.map(g => A.repo + '/' + g).join(', ')}`.
findings.why_it_matters: `latex_source_globs` is documented as a LaTeX-source list, and the design's own example config sets it to `["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]` (ARCHITECTURE.md:1241; another consumer is shown with `["src/*.jl"]` at :1353). For exactly those consumers this edit does not widen the surface, it CUTS it: `docs/src` pages and the `docs/` rationale documents — read by every `needs: source` hat in every panel to date — disappear from what the hat is told to read, while the hat's obligation to quote findings at their source file:line is unchanged. A consumer set to `["src/*.jl"]` loses three of the four surfaces and will report a narrower panel with no signal that anything was withheld. The defect being fixed was the OPPOSITE — a Literate surface never read — and the fix for 'examples/*.jl is missing' is a union with the four defaults, not a replacement. The added `"source_globs"` entry in args.required also makes an args payload without the key invalid, so a round prepared before this commit cannot have its args re-validated as written.
findings.description: One key now carries two different meanings — the LaTeX-notation source list it was defined as, and the whole authored-source substrate of a hat — and the second silently overrides a surface set the consumer never asked to narrow. Nothing warns when the resolved globs omit `docs/src` or `docs/`, and the new test asserts only that `source_globs` is non-empty (`@test !isempty(a["source_globs"]) && a["source_globs"] isa AbstractVector`) over the fixture, whose value is `[]` — i.e. it exercises the default branch only, never the branch that drops surfaces.

["src", "ext", "docs/src", "docs"] : globs`); schema/config.schema.json:441 `"latex_source_globs": {"$ref": "#/$defs/strlist", "default": []}`; ARCHITECTURE.md:1241 `latex_source_globs   = ["src/*.jl", "examples/*.jl"]`; test/coverage.jl:121 renders args over `fixture_config()`, whose `latex_source_globs = []`.

findings.title: The widened waiver resolution silently switches OFF two scans nobody exempted, for ledgers written under the old rule
findings.before: `id = row["id"]; rule = row["rule"]` / `for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")` / `e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)` — exactly one rule, the catalogue's canonical column, could disable a scan.
findings.after: `enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))` / `for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")` / `e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)`
findings.why_it_matters: Run against the real catalogue, the widening attaches a second disabling rule to three scans: RULE.CIT.DOI now disables SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK (the intended repair), but RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE now also disables SCAN.DEAD_REF — every dead cross-reference in the corpus stops being reported — and RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING now also disables SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE. A consumer that wrote either of those two waivers before this commit, for the scan the ledger then actually governed, silently loses enforcement of a rule it never exempted, on a hard-tier scan, with no doctor warning and nothing in `deviations.md` to show the extra withdrawal. The docstring admits the limit — "a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted" — but admitting it does not stop it from happening to ledgers already in the fleet.
findings.description: This is my lens inverted: nothing new is rejected, but previously valid input (an exemptions ledger that used to leave a scan enforcing) now produces a materially weaker result, and the direction of the change is toward silence. The narrow repair for the reported defect — a documented RULE.CIT.DOI waiver being void — is to resolve the waiver and drop only that rule's hits, which the docstring says is impossible because a `Hit` carries no rule id; the shipped alternative buys the DOI half by giving away the DEAD_REF and API_PAGE_STRUCTURE halves. The new test pins that an UNRELATED rule waives nothing (`@test !isempty(G.run_scan(d, row; ledger = pol("RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS")).hits)`) but never asks the question this finding asks — that a SIBLING rule's waiver now disables a scan it did not before.
findings.evidence: `enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))` (Scan.jl:397); executed over the shipped catalogue: SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE canon=RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API newly-resolved=[RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING]; SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK canon=RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE newly-resolved=[RULE.CIT.DOI]; SCAN.DEAD_REF canon=RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS newly-resolved=[RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE]. catalog/scans.toml:7 "`rule` is ONE canonical rule per scan, which is what the ledger and the doctor resolve against."

findings.title: The quantifier class adds ~500 mandatory checklist items corpus-wide — the padding the adjacent comment warns against
findings.before: `ex = occursin(CLAIM_EXIT, s)` / `(ex || occursin(CLAIM_NUMBER, s)) || continue` — two kinds, and the brief told a lane "every CITED NUMBER and every EXIT-CODE CLAIM it found".
findings.after: `qu = occursin(CLAIM_QUANTIFIER, s) && occursin(CLAIM_TOOL_ID, s)` / `(ex || num || qu) || continue`, with `CLAIM_QUANTIFIER = r"\b(?:every|never|always|all|none|any|only)\b"i` and `CLAIM_TOOL_ID = r"…|\bgbg\s+[a-z]+\b"`.
findings.why_it_matters: Measured with the committed regexes over the corpus (.gbg excluded), the quantifier class adds 425 items on `docs/` (1084 -> 1509, +39%), 56 on `src/` and 21 across policy, catalog, instruments, templates and schema. Every item is an obligation the brief makes binding — "An item you leave out of `claims_checked[]` reads as an item you did not check" — carried by lanes that run at economy by default, so the floor under each lane grows by a third to a half for a class that was two planted seeds. The conjunction admits ordinary prose: a sentence containing `only` or `any` anywhere on a line that also contains `gbg round` or a bare `RULE.…` mention matches, whether or not the universal ranges over the tool at all. The author's own comment two lines up states the standard this violates: "a checklist padded with unverifiable items is the shape that got the quantifier class dropped as unaffordable". The same hunk's `CLAIM_EXIT` third alternative, `\bexit\s+contract\b[^.]{0,60}?[0-3]\b`, also matches a version string near the phrase (the `1` of `v1.0.0` ends on a word boundary), which is why it adds items on `src/` and `docs/` but none on the policy tree.
findings.description: The class is worth catching — two of five seeds were quantifier mutations — but the filter shipped is far wider than the seeds it missed, and the cost lands on the lanes as an unbounded per-item verdict obligation at economy strength. A narrower conjunction (the universal and the tool identifier in the same CLAUSE, or the universal governing a named verb or rule) would keep the seeded cases; nothing in the diff measures what the new checklist costs a lane, and the round's own lane briefs were updated only in wording.
findings.evidence: Measured by running the committed regexes with the committed filters (`strip`, `length <= 400`) over the shipped file set: src/ old=167 new=171 quantifier_added=56; docs/ old=1082 new=1084 quantifier_added=425; policy+catalog+instruments+templates+schema old=113 new=113 quantifier_added=21. Comment at Preflight.jl:347-349: "The digit is REQUIRED near the phrase … a checklist padded with unverifiable items is the shape that got the quantifier class dropped as unaffordable."

findings.title: `gbg round build` now mutates ROUND.toml — an undocumented side effect that can make the verb fail where it used to run
findings.before: `function build(cfg, round; io = stdout)` / `guard(cfg, round; io)` / `code = run_under_round(…)` / `println(io, "build: exit $code — $log"); return code` — a read-only verb over the round.
findings.after: `dir, rec = guard(cfg, round; io)` … `rec["build"] = Dict{String,Any}("code" => code, "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40), "at" => timestamp())` / `save(dir, rec)`
findings.why_it_matters: `save` validates the ENTIRE record against round.schema.json and throws `RoundError` when it does not validate, so `gbg round build` — documented as "the consumer's `docs_build` under `GBG_ROUND`, the log under the round's scratch … Returns the command's exit code" — can now fail without ever running a build, for a record an earlier tool version wrote. It also leaves the round directory dirty on every invocation, which close independently refuses ('the round's files are not committed'), so a verb the guide presents as a mid-pass convenience ('A build or test during the pass is `gbg round build <round>`') now obliges a commit. Neither the docstring nor any guide page says the verb writes anything; the docstring's word count is unchanged in docs/prose_shape.csv, confirming the contract was not revisited.
findings.description: Recording the verdict is the right mechanism for the defect, but the verb's documented contract — run, log, return the code — was not updated to say it now persists state into ROUND.toml and validates the whole record while doing so. The new testset pins the recording over a fresh, valid record only; nothing exercises build over a record that fails validation, which is the case where a previously working verb now throws.
